Resolved as an authoring default, 2026-11-03: Brief 2–4 hours, Short 6–24 hours, Standard 2–3 days, Long 5–8 days, Persistent until a named world event; a window runs from the POI's appearance.
Resolved as an authoring default, 2026-11-03: A Marked POI shows its source's words, never a number or countdown; the marker becomes an aftermath mark when the window ends.
Resolved as an authoring default, 2026-11-03: At most three active event POIs a district, at most two Brief or Short; taken tasks and the war's operations do not count.
Resolved as an authoring default, 2026-11-03: About five tips a district a day: two or three morning notices, one evening bartender tip, two or three rumour lines; every POI has two sources.
Resolved as an authoring default, 2026-11-03: A tip Marks when it names a walkable place; two Hinted sources, a found Physical Trace, or entering the area also Mark.

Resolved as an authoring default, 2026-11-03: All sources slant; about one tip in five may be wrong and is contradicted in time; Physical Traces never lie; the slice has at most one false rumour a day.
Resolved as an authoring default, 2026-11-03: A Persistent POI has no clock and ends on a named world event of the war, stated by its sources.
Resolved as an authoring default, 2026-11-03: Limit 8 needs 8 points of Arcana deeds, each kind at most three times; Limit 7 is for NPCs only.

Resolved as an authoring default, 2026-11-03: a fight starts in place with no cut; no interface warning, only diegetic ones; an ambush gives none.

Resolved as an authoring default, 2026-11-03: A diagonal step costs 1 AP, the same as an orthogonal one, as the balance simulations count it.

Resolved as an authoring default, 2026-11-03: Three bands, D 1, 3 and 5, checked against the attribute on the 07.1 curve; AP 2–3; a failure spends the AP and costs position, a fall 10 % of maximum HP per 2 m.

What is the V1 overworld target size (km / play minutes edge-to-edge) beyond the V0 world (2800 × 2800 m / 64 m chunks already locked in 17)? The same entry notes a measured budget: about 2.5–3 km² of dry land fits two large cities; three with real travel between them needs 4–6 km². That means growing the world, not just the island.
When does Piece-Based Assembly fully replace the single hand-placed Interior V0 template scene as authority for Interior Scenes? The mechanism itself is locked; only the V0 to V1 timing is open.
When does additive interior load replace the V0 single-scene swap? The V0 default is locked in 17; the V1 timing is open.

99 holds Stage 3F valley-carve questions 3F-1 through 3F-25. They are research and production-terrain questions. They are not current gameplay-design blockers. Production terrain stays unchanged, Stage 3F stays experimental, and an agent recommendation in that section is not a decision.
What probability distribution assigns major/minor groups within the 3+3 limits, and how does random Enchanting addition choose among groups that have free slots?

Confirm whether base-favored modifier types are independent of major/minor group (the current draft treats them independently). What is the final base catalogue and its favored-type weights, stage/tier tables, numeric ranges, and duplicate constraints?
Which Enchanting skill levels unlock Steps 2–6 after learning Enchanting grants Step 1?
What costs, ingredient lists, stations/requirements, and world-time durations apply to each Enchanting operation?
What are the durability wear rates and exact repair method/station, ordinary-ingredient fraction, and duration? Repair uses no rare ingredients.
Will transformed NPCs exist as monsters, and what items may they drop? What rules govern non-equipment carried goods and other non-combat item acquisition?
What is the home-stash capacity/storage policy, and what are the final equipment slots, compatibility/requirements, and full item weights by base/material/tool/consumable?
Does tier raising advance exactly one tier step, and may it target a locked modifier?
Which items may be stored in or reliably inherited from a Legacy Cache, including extracted modifier instances?
What exact colour values, icons, and accessible UI treatment accompany the agreed item quality colour categories?

How many rituals must the cult complete before the capital? Resolved: no fixed count. The Capital Gate opens when every other city is under Cult Control. Scheduling and concurrency moved to CC-4; difficulty ownership to CC-14.

Which public events enter the daily bulletin and map, how quickly do reports spread, and when does a source reveal an exact ritual site versus only a region? The private daily summary always records the player's own actions; its interface and retention remain open.
Which cult command roles must be removed to complete the campaign before manifestation? Resolved: killing all three Cult Generals is the only way.
Where is the final awakening ritual held? It is fixed at the centre of the capital.
How much can other autonomous practitioners change ritual outcomes? What state triggers the separate planet-destruction rite? Off-screen clashes are tracked as CC-15, allied behaviour as CC-16.
Which actions and scoring weights determine the final campaign rating?
Beyond killing or capturing all responsible ritualists, which non-combat methods can stop a ritual, and what custody, escape, and return-to-cult rules support taking them alive?
After the ending rating, can the surviving character continue in an epilogue or free-play state, and how does that relate to the world's finite life-cycle?
CC-1. Resolved: tempo comes from generation, not a calendar. Numbers belong to CC-12.
CC-2. The target is decided: 3×3 tiles and 5–7 cities, ideally 7. Does the count include the capital, what is the minimum distance between cities, and what terrain plan delivers this?

text: CC-3. Resolved by the owner, 2026-11-03: any initiated character who openly resists counts for capture and liberation, a hidden one never; a lone player can delay a capture by fighting but cannot hold a city by presence.
CC-4. Resolved: order, one-hour window, and garrison sizes are decided.
CC-5. Resolved: a capture ritual makes a city a Place of Power and keeps residents alive as sacrifices. Remaining questions moved to CC-20 and CC-21.

CC-6. Resolved by the owner, 2026-11-03: the patrol's check is an ordinary Social Check with an Argument; shops work with higher prices and poorer stock; a captured city shows patrols, cult signs, closed temples, empty night streets, and no allied banners.
CC-7. Resolved by the owner, 2026-11-03: a sortie against an Unclaimed city with no open resistance needs no fight; a General loses only followers.
CC-8. Resolved by the owner, 2026-11-03: a campaign ritual has two Weak Points at the middle setting and one at higher settings; further kinds come later; traces follow the slice's scheme.
CC-9. Resolved by the owner, 2026-11-03: a fallen General's free followers join the nearest living General, no new followers of its kind appear, and its garrisons remain.

CC-10. Resolved in part by the owner, 2026-11-03: seers in every city sell or share predictions; Generals move through neutral territory with no camp; focused advancement reaches Limit 2–3 within the campaign. Open: what else shows where a moving General walks, and the progression numbers for this pace.
sectionTitle: High Priority — Cult Campaign and City Control

text: CC-11. Resolved: V1 is the one-city slice; allies and enemies may be deeper than the player's stages.
CC-12. Resolved by the owner, 2026-11-03: every campaign number is set and checked with no player; Campaign Numbers V0 stand as authoring defaults until playtest.
CC-13. Resolved by the owner, 2026-11-03: a Major Faction cannot die, because a god oversees it; faction heads stay in the capital and go out rarely, by chance, persuasion, or a Sponsored Operation.
CC-14. Resolved: the eighth slider, Cult Pace, owns campaign pace. Authoring defaults for its range and steps are ×0.5 to ×1.5 in five steps.
CC-15. Resolved by the owner, 2026-11-03: an unseen fight is the same tactical fight without drawing, with the same seed; the agent rebuilds the campaign odds on it.
CC-16. Resolved by the owner, 2026-11-03: the allied factions follow one rule and differ only in starting cities and slightly in fighters by Arcana; they sometimes join attacks.

CC-17. A liberated city whose ritual has neither been undone nor lapsed still counts. How does the final battle with three Generals run, can the smaller rituals be disrupted, how long is the capital ritual, and what follows a broken one? Working model for the simulation in 21 §8: the attack comes a day after the Gate opens, a quarter of the defenders start at the ritual, and a broken ritual is tried again after two days. The owner approved that start at the ritual as the one exception to 21 §4. Owner, 2026-11-03: entrances, gates with hit points, the Spirit General inside first, the main fight on the central square and the ritual at a seed-chosen place away from it, with no physical Weak Point; open: entrances and gate numbers.

text: CC-21. Resolved: the player learns the purpose only at manifestation; a player who wins before it never does.

CC-22. All three cult Arcana have an occupied Limit 0. Which Arcana do the other two Generals belong to, does the World Seed vary which Limit 0 are occupied, and which sources tell the character? Owner, 2026-11-03: ideally three different Arcana; for now all three Generals are on the Emperor.

text: CC-23. Resolved as an authoring default, 2026-11-03: in a tactical fight the cult checks the Force Estimate each round and retreats below 0.15; losses come from the chase, with no fixed share.
CC-24. Resolved: the Spirit General comes out after one to two game days, so a run lasts about 3–6 real hours.

CC-25. Resolved: one rule covers the slice and the campaign. The ritual starts with the attack, and the Spirit General leaves after 15–20 ticks; a General that does not attack is an approved fallback.
CC-26. Resolved: the required mechanics, the one joinable faction, Lower Veil as a district, and the three POIs as side events are decided.

CC-27. Resolved: Limit 9 is certain, Limit 8 takes directed effort, Limit 7 is for NPCs; 8–10 enemies, with allies who stop the ritual about 40 % of the time with no player; the one-hour window stays.
CC-28. Resolved: the character starts without a faction and may join through a first-day trial; death ends the run.

CC-29. Resolved in principle: the slice's 12 abilities are in 05.1, cult followers use only Император and allies only Жрица, every character starts Uninitiated and Factionless, and the city is Veilmouth.
CC-30. Resolved: Arcana and Limit are the only terms, and there are no path names.
CC-31. All 220 Limit names are unique and the secondary attribute is fixed per Arcana. Four attribute profiles are still identical and are resolved with CC-35.

text: CC-32. Resolved: the world lives one tick per round, ordinary NPCs hide, defenders go to the fight, and a character leaves it about 10 cells from the nearest enemy.
